# Document 1 & 2: Information Sheet + Consent {background-color="#275882"}

## Participant Information Sheet

::: {.definition-box}
**What it is:** A formal document explaining the study to potential participants *before* they agree. Required for informed consent.

**Tips:** Describe the study in general terms — do **not** reveal your hypothesis. Include: purpose, what participation involves, time, risks/benefits, confidentiality, right to withdraw. Use the template and customise the "purpose" and "what will happen" sections.
:::

---

## Consent Form

::: {.definition-box}
**What it is:** The checklist the participant signs to confirm they understand and agree. Legal and ethical requirement.

**Tips:** Update the **study title** to match across all documents. The checklist items are standard. Print plenty of spare copies (aim for 30).
:::

---

## Activity: Info Sheet + Consent

::: {.exercise-box}
**In your group (25–30 min):**

1. Open the **template** (or example) from the [Project Toolkit](project/project-toolkit.qmd).
2. Draft the **Participant Information Sheet**: purpose, what will happen, time, right to withdraw, confidentiality.
3. Draft the **Consent Form**: same study title everywhere.
4. Save in a shared folder; one person can take the lead.
:::

---

# Document 3 & 7: Debrief + Instructions {background-color="#275882"}

## Debrief Form

::: {.definition-box}
**What it is:** Given *after* the study. Explains true purpose, hypothesis, and theory.

**Tips:** Here you **can** (and should) reveal the hypothesis. Briefly explain the theory. Include data withdrawal instructions and support contacts. About one page.
:::

---

## Participant Instructions

::: {.definition-box}
**What it is:** Step-by-step sheet telling the participant exactly what to do during the study.

**Tips:** Plain language, numbered steps. Do **not** reveal the hypothesis. Keep short (about half a page). Different procedures for between vs within may need separate instruction sheets.
:::

---

## Activity: Debrief + Participant Instructions

::: {.exercise-box}
**In your group (25–30 min):**

1. Draft the **Debrief Form**: true purpose, hypothesis, theory, withdrawal info, support.
2. Draft **Participant Instructions**: what the participant does, in order, in simple language.
3. Check: no hypothesis in the instructions; hypothesis is in the debrief.
:::

---

# Document 8: Researcher Procedure (Start) {background-color="#275882"}

## Researcher Procedure

::: {.definition-box}
**What it is:** Your detailed "recipe" for running the study. Researchers only. Includes exact wording, timing, and full procedure.

**Tips:** Be very detailed — exact words to say (in quotes/italics). Include timing for each phase. Include a checklist of materials to prepare. Any group member should be able to run the study from this alone.
:::

---

## What to Include (Start Today)

- **Checklist**: What to prepare before testing (forms, stimuli, timer, etc.)
- **Opening**: What you say when you greet the participant
- **Order of steps**: Consent → Instructions → [your task] → Debrief
- **Timing**: How long for study phase, distractor, recall, etc.
- **Exact script**: Key phrases participants hear (in quotes)

You will **complete** this document in Week 18 (Phase 2).

---

## Activity: Start Researcher Procedure

::: {.exercise-box}
**In your group (25–30 min):**

1. Open the **Researcher Procedure** template from the Project Toolkit.
2. Write the **materials checklist** (everything you need on the day).
3. Write the **sequence**: greeting → consent → instructions → main task (with timings) → debrief.
4. Add **exact wording** for the key instructions you will read to participants.
5. Save; you will finalise and add data-recording details in Week 18.
:::
